heading: The week in short
body:
OP-18 is out in English and Japanese, and it is now the One Piece story: older boxes are being sold off (OP-17 is −15% over four weeks, OP-09 −14%) and the OP-05 spike from last week has faded to −8%. In Pokémon the 30th Celebration chase cards are still sliding gently (Mew ex 152 €76.60, −7% against its 30-day average) while Mega Darkrai ex 116 from Pitch Black is the one chase card going up (+6%, €183.58). Your collection fell on paper, about 16% to €51.60, almost all of it from five Japanese cards whose price source dropped (see Your collection). We still cannot confirm results for the One Piece Regionals of 7 to 21 November or for Chiba.

What to do: hold your 30th Celebration singles and keep buying slowly. Don't buy OP-17 or OP-09 boxes yet. If you want OP-18 sealed, compare Réunion shop prices with the $4.99 English booster price before paying a launch premium.

heading: OP-18 is out: what we know
body:
English release was Friday 20 November and Japanese Saturday 21 November (Bandai pages, via Samurai Sword Tokyo). Each pack has 12 cards and each box 24 packs; English packs retail at $4.99. French retailers say 20 November with a 24-booster display, but Bandai has not given a French date, so treat that as unconfirmed. Play-in listed French pre-release events from 21 November at €35 for 6 boosters.

The top chase card named by Samurai Sword Tokyo is Nico Robin Super Alt Art (OP18-031); Saint Gunko's Holy Knights alt art (OP18-065) is quoted at $19.90. That site also says the Amano attribution comes from media reports, not Bandai's product pages, and there is no sale history yet, so early asking prices are guesses. Tournament legality is reported as 27 November (the site's own count of seven days).

What to do: wait two to three weeks for singles prices to settle. Buying a few packs for fun is fine; buying a box for profit at launch prices rarely works.

heading: Sealed boxes: the OP-05 spike fades
body:
Japanese booster-box prices (eBay sold medians, opboxindex, 22 November): OP-05 $194 (−7.6% over four weeks; last week it showed +22% at $213), OP-10 $100 (+15%, median dated 13 Nov), OP-17 $100 (−14.5%, last week −13%), OP-09 $109 (−14%, last week −23%), EB-02 $159 (+18%, dated 10 Nov). The page gave no OP-18 or OP-02 figures this week.

EB-02 has swung between −26% and +18% in two weeks, so it is thin sales, not a trend. OP-05 jumping then dropping the same way says: don't chase these spikes.

What to do: OP-17 is still falling as OP-18 takes attention; wait. If you hold OP-05 sealed, last week's price was the better moment to sell, but one week is noise.

heading: 30th Celebration: still sliding, slowly; Darkrai rising
body:
Cardmarket via TCGdex, read 23 November (7-day average against 30-day): Mew ex 152 €76.60 (−7%), Pikachu ex 150 €47.14 (trend; 7-day €46.65 vs 30-day €49.81, −6%), Mewtwo ex 151 €41.40 (−8%), Gengar ex 154 €60.72 (−3%), Jirachi ex 155 €29.52 (−4%), Greninja ex 148 €14.81 (−9%), Sylveon ex 153 €29.07 (−8%), Salamence ex 156 €14.47 (−7%). Meowth 144 and Maushold 146 are −18% and −20% but only €3.75 to €4.11. Compared with last week's prices, Mew ex fell from €79.66 and Mewtwo ex from €43.96, so the drop is steady, not a crash.

Mega Darkrai ex 116 (Pitch Black) is €183.58, with the 7-day average €188.96 above the 30-day €178.59 (+6%). Morpeko ex 117 is flat at €48.22 (trend; 7-day €49.09 vs 30-day €48.12).

What to do: still hold. A floor may be near, but buying one card at a time is safer than all at once.

heading: Règne Delta in Réunion: mostly in stock
body:
Miyata Kard Market lists French Règne Delta (ME06): booster €7.99, three-pack €19.99, 6-booster bundle €44.99 (was €49.99), 36-booster display €239.99. Only the Elite Trainer Box (€79.99, was €89.99) is clearly marked sold out; the page's stock labels are inconsistent, so check each product page. The shop is open Tuesday to Saturday, 13:00 to 18:00. Planet Geek lists the ME06 booster at €7.99 and a booster bundle at €59.99, and for One Piece the OP17 French booster at €9.49, EB05 display €229.99 and OP17 double pack €19.99 (no stock levels shown).

The bundle is €10.05 cheaper at Miyata (€44.99 vs €59.99). Per pack the Miyata display is €6.67 (€239.99 ÷ 36).

Mega Rayquaza ex prices are still not trustworthy: we did not re-check them this week.

heading: Championships: LAIC and Chiba
body:
Pokémon: Limitless shows Latin America Internationals in São Paulo (20 to 22 November) won by Vinícius Fernandez (BR) with 2,646 players, and Buenos Aires (14 November) won by Calvin Connor (US) with 553 players. We did not find the winning decks. Some search results name Pedro Pertusi, but that is from the 2025 event, so ignore it. Champions League Chiba was played on 22 November; no result found yet.

Meta (Limitless, TEF-DLR format): Dragapult ex 35.7%, Basic Box 11.6%, N's Zoroark ex 8.9%, Slowking 8.4%, Crustle 5.9%, Mega Excadrill ex 4.5%, Hydrapple ex 4.1%. Last week Dragapult was 36.5% and Basic Box 8.9%.

One Piece: Limitless's results page still ends on 26 July, so we cannot confirm Porto, Sydney, Oklahoma City (21 November) or Bristol. The meta table (Nami 23.5%, Luffy 22.9%, Enel 22.7%) is the OP16 format and is not current for OP-17 or OP-18.

Next: Regional Stuttgart (Pokémon) and Regional Alicante (One Piece), both 28 November.

heading: Your collection
body:
Rebuilt on 23 November: 95 of 122 cards priced, listed value €51.60 against €61.56 last week (about −16%). Rate used: Rs 51.30 per euro (last week 52.53; open.er-api.com, because valutafx blocked the request). That alone is about −2% in rupees.

Most of the fall is five cards: Dragonite 149/165 (JP 151) €4.33 to €0.88, Dragonair 148/165 €3.58 to €2.06, Charizard ex 006/165 €3.17 to €2.11, Pikachu 025/165 €3.05 to €1.26 and Luffy OP15-119 €2.83 to €1.84. Four are Japanese 151 cards, and a fall that large in one week looks more like a price-source change than a market move, so we have not confirmed it. Treat it with caution.

Top cards: Albia 109/084 €6.27, Flagadoss 090/084 €5.43, Arcanine 059/165 €4.41, Hitmonlee 107/165 €4.06 (Rising), Clefable 036/165 €2.89 (Rising).

What to do: nothing to sell. The whole collection is worth less than one Elite Trainer Box. Keep the Rising cards.

heading: Language gaps
body: No comparable English, French and Japanese prices this week. Cardmarket pools languages and TCGdex still returns placeholders for Règne Delta. One real gap: the English OP-18 booster is $4.99 retail, while Planet Geek's French OP17 booster is €9.49 and its French ME06 Pokémon booster €7.99 (different sets, so not a like-for-like comparison). Last week's Mega Rayquaza and Xebec Manga figures were not re-checked.

heading: Your Réunion window: 34 days left
body:
You have 34 days on the island until 27 December. This week: (1) Miyata Kard Market, Saint-Louis: Règne Delta bundle €44.99 and display €239.99; ETB sold out. (2) Planet Geek (closed Monday and Tuesday): French OP17 and EB05 stock, ME06 booster €7.99. (3) PUNK Records, Le Tampon: runs One Piece tournaments; ask about OP-18 (0693 00 31 81). (4) Sortilèges' site shows no prices; call before travelling.

Buy the sealed French products you want before 27 December; after that you will be buying from Mauritius.
source: Miyata; Planet Geek; PUNK Records; Sortilèges

heading: Coming up
body: 28 Nov: Regional Stuttgart (Pokémon) and Regional Alicante (One Piece); OP-18 cards legal about 27 Nov. 27 Nov: Pokémon Aura Seeker (Japan, date reported, not official). 5 Dec: Pokémon Las Vegas; One Piece Munich and others. 12 Dec: One Piece Paris. 18 to 19 Dec: One Piece ST-37 and ST-38. 2027: Flowing Fists (English Aura Seeker) on 5 or 6 Feb (sources conflict, unconfirmed); Valentine's box 27 Jan (reported).

heading: About the numbers
body: Euro prices come from Cardmarket via TCGdex, read 23 November; movers compare 7-day with 30-day averages, and I checked only the 30th Celebration and Pitch Black cards. One Piece box prices are eBay sold medians in dollars from opboxindex (no MUR shown because no dollar rate was sourced). Rate Rs 51.30 per euro. Unconfirmed: all One Piece results since July, Chiba result, LAIC deck, French OP-18 date, Aura Seeker dates, EB-02 and the Japanese 151 card price drops. Collection: 95 of 122 priced.
